attempts.summary: Segmented node2 onto VLAN 10 and node3 onto VLAN 20 as 802.1Q sub-interfaces over the shared eth1 link, with node1 (VyOS) routing between the two VLANs. node1: eth1 vif 10 = 10.10.10.254/24, vif 20 = 10.10.20.254/24 (committed and saved). node2: eth1.10 = 10.10.10.11/24 with a specific route to 10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.254. node3: eth1.20 = 10.10.20.12/24 with a specific route to 10.10.10.0/24 via 10.10.20.254 (specific routes chosen over a full default-route gateway so node2/node3 keep their existing internet egress via eth0). Verified bidirectional cross-VLAN ping with ttl=63 confirming a routed hop through node1, and that internet egress was undisturbed. Then performed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes (node1, then node2, then node3): captured baseline boot_id per node, triggered a background-scheduled native reboot on each, polled until the node's command execution returned, confirmed a new boot_id proving a genuine restart, and verified VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN connectivity fully recovered after each restart before moving to the next node.
